scenes.heading: Perimeter and circles
scenes.sub: Straight edges, curved edges, and π
scenes.say: How far is it around a running track? Part of it is straight and part of it is curved. In this lesson you'll learn to find the perimeter of any shape, curved bits included.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Walk around a playground with one hand on the fence
scenes.science: Perimeter = total distance around the outside edge
scenes.breaks: A real fence has thickness; in maths the edge is a perfect line with no width.
scenes.say: Imagine walking right around a playground with one hand on the fence. The perimeter is how far you walk. If the fence curves, you still walk along it, and pi helps with that part. You never walk across the middle, so lines inside the shape don't count.

scenes.heading: Circumference
scenes.say: The perimeter of a circle is called its circumference. It equals pi times the diameter, or two pi r. Always check whether you have been given the radius or the diameter.

scenes.heading: A sector is a slice of a circle
scenes.say: First the whole circle, dashed. Then a slice: two radii and a curved arc. The angle theta at the centre tells you what fraction of the circle you have. The arc length is theta over three sixty times two pi r. For the perimeter, add the two straight radii.
scenes.caption: The angle θ tells you the fraction of the circle. Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr. For the perimeter, add the two radii.

scenes.heading: Sector perimeter
scenes.question: Find the perimeter of a sector with radius 6 cm and angle 120°, to 1 decimal place.
scenes.say: A sector has radius six centimetres and angle one hundred and twenty degrees. That is one third of the circle. The arc is one third of two pi times six, about twelve point five seven. Add the two radii and the perimeter is about twenty-four point six centimetres.
scenes.caption: 120° is ⅓ of the circle. Arc = ⅓ × 2π × 6 ≈ 12.57 cm. Add the two radii: perimeter ≈ 24.6 cm.

scenes.heading: Two semicircles make one circle
scenes.say: Here's a running track. First the outline, then the two straights of eighty metres. Each end is a semicircle with diameter fifty metres. Two semicircles make one whole circle, so the ends add up to pi times fifty. The dashed lines are inside, so leave them out. The total is about three hundred and seventeen point one metres.
scenes.caption: Two straights of 80 m. Each end is a semicircle with diameter 50 m; together they make one circle: π × 50. Leave out the dashed lines. Total ≈ 317.1 m.

scenes.heading: What goes in the perimeter?

right.title: Leave it out
points: Lines where you split a shape

scenes.say: Count every edge on the outside: arcs, the straight radii of a sector, and the diameter of a semicircle. Leave out dashed lines inside the shape, and do not use area formulas.

Quick recap. Perimeter means adding every outside edge. Circumference is pi d. Arc length is theta over three sixty times two pi r, and a sector’s perimeter adds two radii. Round only at the end. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Perimeter: add every outside edge. C = πd. Arc = θ/360 × 2πr. Sector perimeter = arc + 2r. Round only at the end. Now try the practice questions!
